Download hangs, E204 at 60 s, tab hidden at 90 s and shown at 100 s: SPEC sends a second E204 (reading a at 160 s, reading b at 100 s); FIX sends one. The same with a pause before the firing (E204 at 120 s, hide/show at 130/140 s): SPEC sends a second E204 (160 s / 140 s); FIX one. The three section 6 cases (two hidden minutes; 40 s visible, 60 s hidden, 20 s visible; a render, then hide and show) give the same result in SPEC and FIX: none, one at 120 s, none. A font that arrives at 70 s after an E204 still clears the banner in FIX. jsdom 29.1.1 has no document.fonts (typeof is 'undefined'). before.text:
**E204 counts visible time only.** AlphaTab 1.8.4 starts its first render from an animation
frame, and a browser runs none in a hidden tab, so a player opened in a background tab draws
nothing there while a plain timer keeps counting. The 60 seconds therefore run only while
`document.visibilityState` is `visible`: a player opened in a background tab starts the clock when
the tab is first shown, a `visibilitychange` to `hidden` stops it, it continues with the time left
when the page is visible again, and the first `renderFinished` stops it for good, so a later tab
switch never starts it again. Without this, a background tab left for a minute sends an unhandled
E204 that lowers the health number although nothing failed.

- **The font clock**, a test beside `web/app/play/NotationSurface.tsx`, with fake timers and a
  stubbed `document.visibilityState`: two hidden minutes raise no E204; 40 visible seconds, a hidden
  minute, then 20 more visible seconds raise one; and once a render has finished, hiding and showing
  the tab raises none a minute later. The end-to-end lane cannot cover this: headless Chromium keeps
  every page visible.

after_draft.option: 1 (recommended by verification: DES-1's rule, plus why an E203 ends the clock and the banner sentence)
after_draft.text:
**E204 counts visible time only.** AlphaTab 1.8.4 starts its first render from an animation
frame, and a browser runs none in a hidden tab, so a player opened in a background tab draws
nothing there while a plain timer keeps counting. The 60 seconds therefore run only while
`document.visibilityState` is `visible`: a player opened in a background tab starts the clock when
the tab is first shown, a `visibilitychange` to `hidden` stops it, and it continues with the time
left when the page is visible again. Without this, a background tab left for a minute sends an
unhandled E204 that lowers the health number although nothing failed.

**Three events stop the clock permanently.** The first finished render, an E203, or the E204
itself stops it, and after that a tab switch never starts it again. An E203 stops it because
AlphaTab never draws once the font download has failed: without this, every E203 would be
followed by a second unhandled report when the 60 visible seconds end, an E204 that says the font
is late when it has already failed. The same clock also sets the banner's E204 text, so after an
E203 the banner keeps its E203 text, and the clock does not show it again after the visitor
dismisses it.

after_draft.option: 2 (DES-1's own suggested wording, in place: the reviewers' recommendation)

when the page is visible again, and the clock ends for good at the first of three events: a

itself, so a later tab switch can never start it again. Without this, a background tab left for a

items.scenario: You open /play on a weak hotel network, the music-font download fails, and the banner reads 'Error E203: the music font could not be downloaded'; you dismiss it. About a minute later the banner returns, now reading 'Error E204: the music font did not arrive within 60 seconds', and the owner's Sentry gains a second issue, with its own email, saying the download hung when it failed. On another visit the download really hangs and E204 is sent at 60 seconds; you switch to another tab and back, and a literal reading of 'it continues with the time left' sends E204 again.
items.corrections: None of substance. Two precisions: the second new-issue email arrives once, when the E204 issue is first created (later failed visits add events to that issue); and the health number does not drop twice, because the session is already unhandled after the E203. Whether a second E204 follows a tab switch depends on how the implementer reads 'the time left' (the model shows both natural readings send it), so it is a gap in the text rather than a certain bug.
items.notes_for_triage: Completes F-29 (lap 2), whose text named only renderFinished. The reviewers recommended the rule in DES-1's own words (option 2). Verification recommends option 1, which makes the same rule but gives it its own paragraph, says why an E203 ends the clock, and adds the banner sentence the scope-guardian's note asks for; option 2 keeps the idiom 'for good' and puts two colons in one sentence. The banner sentence matters because one timer drives both the report and the banner (web/app/play/NotationSurface.tsx:125-130): without it, an implementer could keep a wall-clock timer for the banner and change only the report, and the section 6 case could not tell. The fix changes what a visitor sees: today, before this spec, the banner already switches from E203 to E204 after 60 s and returns after a dismissal (the TODAY model); with the fix it keeps the E203 text. No e2e case waits 60 s after a font abort (web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:215-223 checks E203 soon after load), so none breaks. Reverse order stays as it is: a download that hangs past 60 visible seconds and then fails sends E204, then E203, both true, and the banner switches to E203. The section 6 draft also adds 'a stub document.fonts (jsdom has none)': that is a verification addition, not part of DES-1 — the component's effect calls document.fonts.addEventListener on mount (NotationSurface.tsx:121), which throws in jsdom without a stub, for the three existing cases as well; the stub is also how the new E203 case raises its event. 'Permanently' means for the life of that player, as 'for good' does today: the clock lives in an effect keyed on the AlphaTab api (NotationSurface.tsx:107-136), so a new player after leaving /play and coming back starts a new clock. What a Drop leaves: every failed font download sends a false E204 when the 60 visible seconds end, and the clock's behaviour after an E204 is left to the implementer.

items.scenario: You, the owner, scan your inbox for Sentry alerts and find two new-issue emails whose subjects read 'WEB-4 - Error' and 'WEB-7 - Error' (the short IDs here are examples). One is a file over 25 MB (E101) and one a file that is not a score (E103), but nothing in the subject says which. You open each email or issue and look for the `code` tag before you can decide which one needs you.

after_draft.text:
**Changed files:** `web/next.config.ts` (the `withSentryConfig` wrapper), `web/package.json` (the
dependency, and the token check at the end of its `build` script), both `error.tsx` files, the 16
catch sites and 4 failure paths listed in section 2.4, `web/app/page.tsx` (copy),
`web/eslint.config.mjs` (the rule), `web/AGENTS.md` (the rule, in words), `web/e2e/page-errors.ts`
(reads the shared list), the `/` screenshot baseline, `web/README.md` (the environment variables),
`web/playwright.e2e.config.ts` (a fake DSN), `cspell.json`, and the decision registry and
changelog. Also:

- `web/README.md` — the Deploy section names both environment variables.
- `web/AGENTS.md` — one bullet in its "This package" list, beside the AlphaTab import fence: every
  `catch` and `.catch()` callback in `web/` calls `reportError` or `noteError` from
  `web/lib/monitoring/report.ts`, a deliberate silence is
  `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax -- <reason>`, and lint enforces the rule
  (section 2.5).

items.scenario: You, the next agent, add `try { … } catch { setFailed(true) }` to a new component in web/. You read web/AGENTS.md, the package's own contract, and it lists the AlphaTab import fence but nothing about catches, so you learn the rule only when pnpm run lint fails with no-restricted-syntax, and the exact opt-out comment is written only in this spec.
items.notes_for_triage: Optional, not in the reviewer's text: the bullet could also say that the browser's own global reportError is banned (no-restricted-globals, section 2.5), the other trap an agent meets. What a Drop leaves: nothing breaks; the rule is learned from a lint failure.
